senses.def: lasting or existing for the whole of your life
examples: They met in college and became lifelong friends.
His lifelong dream was to sail around the world.

note: Used before a noun only: a lifelong fan.

senses.def: the way a person or group lives, including their habits and the things they own
examples: Doctors recommend a healthier lifestyle with more exercise.
Moving to the countryside changed their whole lifestyle.

senses.def: the length of time that someone lives or something lasts
examples: Technology changed enormously during my grandmother's lifetime.
The battery has a lifetime of about five years.

note: "Once-in-a-lifetime" describes a very rare opportunity.

senses.def: to move something or someone to a higher position
examples: Can you help me lift this box onto the shelf?
She lifted the baby out of the car seat.

senses.def: to remove a rule or restriction
examples: The government lifted the ban on public gatherings.

senses.def: a free ride in someone's car, or (British) an elevator
examples: Can you give me a lift to the airport?
We took the lift to the fifth floor.

note: For the machine, Americans say "elevator"; "lift" is British. Americans also say "ride" more than "lift" for a car trip.

senses.def: the energy from the sun or a lamp that lets you see, or a device that produces it
examples: The room gets a lot of natural light in the morning.
Turn off the lights when you leave.

senses.def: not heavy
examples: This laptop is light enough to carry all day.
I'll just have a light lunch today.

senses.def: pale in color, or bright with natural light
examples: She was wearing a light blue dress.

senses.def: to make something start to burn, or to give light to a place
examples: It took us half an hour to light a fire with the wet wood.
The streets were lit by old gas lamps.

note: Verb past: lit (or lighted). "In light of" = considering. "Shed light on" = help explain.

senses.def: the type or arrangement of lights in a place
examples: The restaurant has soft, warm lighting.
Poor lighting in the parking lot makes people feel unsafe.

note: Don't confuse with "lightning" (şimşek, yıldırım).

senses.def: to find someone or something pleasant or enjoyable
examples: I really like this neighborhood.
Do you like working from home?

senses.def: used with "would" to say politely what you want
examples: I'd like a table for two, please.
Would you like some coffee?

senses.def: similar to someone or something, or in the same way as
examples: She looks just like her mother.
It tastes like chicken.

senses.def: the things that you enjoy, or a click showing approval online
examples: Tell me about your likes and dislikes.
The video got thousands of likes in an hour.

note: "Feel like doing" = want to do (canı istemek). "What is she like?" asks about character, not preferences.

senses.def: the chance of something happening
examples: Regular exercise reduces the likelihood of heart disease.
There's little likelihood that the bill will pass this year.

note: "In all likelihood" = very probably.

senses.def: probably going to happen or be true
examples: It's likely to rain later this afternoon.
The most likely cause of the fire was a faulty wire.

senses.def: probably
examples: She'll most likely be late again.

note: Pattern: "be likely to do": He is likely to win. As an adverb, usually with "most", "very" or "quite".

senses.def: in the same way
examples: She worked hard, and her children did likewise.
Prices rose sharply in March; likewise, rents went up.

senses.def: used in reply to show you feel the same
examples: "Nice to meet you." "Likewise."

note: Formal as a linking word; informal as a short reply.

senses.def: an arm or a leg, or a similar part of an animal such as a wing
examples: The soldier lost a limb in the explosion.
After the long flight, my limbs felt stiff.

senses.def: a large branch of a tree
examples: A heavy limb fell from the oak during the storm.

note: The b is silent: /lɪm/. "Go out on a limb" = say or do something risky that others may not support.

senses.def: the greatest or smallest amount allowed or possible
examples: The speed limit here is 25 miles per hour.
There's a limit to how much I can help you.

senses.def: to stop something from going beyond a certain amount or level
examples: Try to limit your screen time before bed.
The museum limits the number of visitors each day.

note: "Off limits" = not allowed to be entered or used.

senses.def: the act of controlling or limiting something, or a rule that does this
examples: The treaty called for the limitation of nuclear weapons.
There are strict limitations on how the money can be spent.

senses.def: a weakness or limit on what someone or something can do
examples: Every research method has its limitations.
It's important to know your own limitations.

senses.def: not very large in amount or degree
examples: Seating is limited, so book your tickets early.
We only have a limited amount of time.

note: "Limited edition" = only a small number made. In names, "Limited" (Ltd.) is British; Americans use "Inc."

senses.def: a long, thin mark on a surface
examples: Draw a straight line across the page.
The ball was just over the line.

senses.def: a row of people or things waiting one behind the other
examples: We waited in line for an hour to get tickets.
There's always a long line at the post office.

senses.def: a row of words on a page, words spoken by an actor, or a phone connection
examples: She forgot her lines in the middle of the play.
The line went dead before I could answer.

senses.def: to form rows along the side of something, or to cover the inside of something
examples: Thousands of fans lined the streets for the parade.
Line the baking tray with parchment paper.

note: Americans "wait in line"; British people "queue". "Draw the line" = set a limit you won't go beyond.

senses.def: the people or acts taking part in an event, or a team's selected players
examples: The festival announced an impressive line-up of bands this year.
The coach made three changes to the starting line-up.

senses.def: a row of people shown to a witness who must identify a criminal
examples: The witness picked the suspect out of a police line-up.

note: Often written "lineup" in American English. The verb is two words: line up.

senses.def: in lines, or progressing in a straight, step-by-step way from one stage to the next
examples: The movie doesn't follow a linear storyline.
Career paths are much less linear than they used to be.

senses.def: showing a relationship in which one value changes in direct proportion to another
examples: The graph shows a linear relationship between price and demand.

senses.def: to continue to exist for longer than expected
examples: The smell of smoke lingered in the house for days.
Doubts about his honesty still linger.

senses.def: to stay somewhere longer than necessary because you don't want to leave
examples: We lingered over coffee long after the meal was finished.

senses.def: a connection between two or more people, things or ideas
examples: Scientists have found a link between sugar and heart disease.
The two countries have strong trade links.

senses.def: a word or image on a web page that takes you to another page when you click it
examples: Click the link in the email to reset your password.

senses.def: to connect two or more things, physically, electronically or in your mind
examples: The study linked air pollution to asthma in children.
A new bridge will link the island to the mainland.

note: "The weakest link" = the weakest part of a system or team.

senses.def: a large, powerful wild cat with yellow-brown fur that lives in Africa and parts of Asia
examples: We watched a lion hunting zebras on the safari.
The male lion has a thick mane around its neck.

note: "The lion's share" = the largest part of something.

senses.def: either of the two soft edges around the opening of the mouth
examples: She put on red lipstick and pressed her lips together.
My lips get dry and cracked in winter.

senses.def: the edge of a cup, bowl or other container
examples: Coffee spilled over the lip of the mug.

note: "My lips are sealed" = I won't tell the secret. "Lip service" = support in words only.

senses.def: a substance that flows freely, like water or oil, and is not a solid or a gas
examples: You can't take liquids over 3.4 ounces through airport security.
Drink plenty of liquids when you have a fever.

senses.def: in the form of a liquid
examples: Use liquid soap instead of a bar.
The rocket runs on liquid oxygen.

senses.def: easily changed into cash
examples: The company has plenty of liquid assets to cover its debts.

senses.def: a series of names, items or numbers written one below the other
examples: I made a shopping list before going to the store.
Her name was on the list of winners.

senses.def: to write or say things in a particular order, or to include something on a list
examples: Please list your previous jobs on the form.
The hotel is listed as one of the best in the city.

senses.def: to pay attention to someone or something that you can hear
examples: I like to listen to podcasts on my way to work.
Are you even listening to me?

senses.def: to take notice of what someone says and do what they advise
examples: I told him not to buy that car, but he wouldn't listen.

note: Use "to" before the object: listen to music, not "listen music". The t is silent: /ˈlɪsn/.

senses.def: a person who listens, especially to the radio or a podcast
examples: The radio show has more than a million listeners.
She's a good listener, so people often share their problems with her.

senses.def: a published list, or one item in a list, such as a property or product for sale
examples: I found the apartment through an online listing.
Check the TV listings to see what's on tonight.

senses.def: the fact of a company's shares being traded on a stock exchange
examples: The startup is planning a listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

senses.def: a metric unit for measuring liquid, equal to about 2.1 American pints
examples: The car's fuel tank holds 50 liters.
Buy a two-liter bottle of soda for the party.

note: British spelling: litre. In everyday US life, gallons and ounces are more common than liters.

senses.def: the ability to read and write
examples: The program aims to improve literacy among adults.
The country's literacy rate has risen to 95 percent.

senses.def: knowledge and skill in a particular area
examples: Schools are starting to teach financial literacy and media literacy.

senses.def: in the exact, basic meaning of the word
examples: The name of the town literally means "red river".
Don't take everything he says literally.

senses.def: used to emphasize something, even when it is not really true (informal)
examples: I was literally dying of boredom in that meeting.

note: The emphasizing use is very common in speech but annoys some people; avoid it in formal writing.

senses.def: connected with literature or with writing books
examples: The novel won a major literary prize.
She works as a literary agent in New York.

senses.def: typical of the style of language used in literature rather than everyday speech
examples: The word "steed" sounds quite literary today.

note: Don't confuse literary (edebi), literal (gerçek anlamda) and literate (okuryazar).

senses.def: written works such as novels, plays and poems that are valued as art
examples: She majored in English literature in college.
The book is considered a classic of American literature.

senses.def: pieces of writing on a particular subject, or printed information about a product
examples: There is a large body of literature on childhood obesity.
Ask the salesperson for some literature about the car.

note: Uncountable. In academic English, "the literature" means published research on a topic (literature review).

senses.def: small pieces of trash such as paper, cans and bottles left lying in public places
examples: The park was covered in litter after the concert.
You can be fined for dropping litter.

senses.def: a group of baby animals born to one mother at the same time
examples: Our dog had a litter of six puppies.

senses.def: to leave trash somewhere, or to be spread untidily over a place
examples: Clothes littered the floor of his bedroom.

note: "Litter box" = the box of sand indoor cats use (kedi kumu kabı).

senses.def: small in size, or young
examples: They live in a little house near the beach.
My little brother just started kindergarten.

senses.tr: (a little) biraz; (little) çok az, pek az
senses.def: a small amount of; without "a", not much or almost no
examples: Add a little salt to the water.
There's little hope of finding survivors now.

senses.def: a small amount, or not much
examples: I understood very little of what he said.

senses.def: to a small degree, or hardly at all
examples: I'm a little tired after the trip.
Little did she know that her life was about to change.

note: "A little" is positive (some); "little" is negative (almost none). Comparative: less, least.

senses.def: to have your home in a particular place
examples: We live in a small apartment downtown.
Where do your parents live now?

senses.def: to be alive, or to have a particular kind of life
examples: My grandfather lived to the age of 98.
They live a quiet, simple life.

senses.def: alive, or happening or broadcast at the same time as it is seen or heard
examples: The restaurant serves live lobsters.
The band played live music all night.

senses.def: broadcast or performed while the event is actually happening
examples: The final will be shown live on TV.

note: Verb is /lɪv/; adjective and adverb are /laɪv/. "Live on" = use as your money or food: live on $1,000 a month.

senses.def: full of life and energy; active and enthusiastic
examples: The neighborhood has a lively nightlife with lots of bars.
She's a lively, outgoing child.

senses.def: involving a lot of strong opinions and interesting ideas
examples: The panel led to a lively debate about immigration.

note: It looks like an adverb but is an adjective. Pronounced /ˈlaɪvli/.

senses.def: a large organ in the body that cleans the blood, or the liver of an animal eaten as food
examples: Heavy drinking can cause serious liver damage.
She ordered fried liver with onions.

note: Turkish "ciğer" can mean lungs or liver; in English these are different: lung = akciğer, liver = karaciğer.

senses.def: money to buy the things you need, or the way you earn it
examples: What does she do for a living?
It's hard to make a living as an artist.

senses.def: a particular way or standard of life
examples: The cost of living in big cities keeps rising.

senses.def: alive now, or still used or existing
examples: She is one of the greatest living writers.
Bacteria are tiny living organisms.

note: "What do you do for a living?" is the natural way to ask about someone's job.

senses.def: something heavy that is carried, often in large amounts
examples: The truck was carrying a load of bricks.
I do three loads of laundry every weekend.

senses.tr: iş yükü, sorumluluk; (a load of) bir sürü
senses.def: an amount of work or responsibility, or (informal) a lot of something
examples: Teachers have a heavy work load this term.
We've got loads of food left over.

senses.def: to put a large amount of things into a vehicle or container, or to put data into a computer
examples: They loaded the car with camping gear.
The page takes forever to load.

note: "Loaded" (informal) can mean very rich. "A loaded question" contains a hidden trap.

senses.def: money that a bank or person lends and that must be paid back, usually with interest
examples: They took out a loan to buy a new car.
It took me ten years to pay off my student loans.

senses.def: the act of lending something
examples: The painting is on loan from a museum in Paris.

senses.def: to lend something, especially money
examples: My uncle loaned me the money for the down payment.

note: As a verb, "loan" is common in American English; British English prefers "lend".

senses.def: a large area inside the entrance of a hotel or public building
examples: I'll meet you in the hotel lobby at seven.
There's a small café in the lobby of the office building.

senses.def: a group of people who try to influence politicians on a particular issue
examples: The gun lobby is very powerful in Washington.

senses.def: to try to persuade politicians or officials to support or oppose a law
examples: Environmental groups are lobbying Congress to cut emissions.
Parents lobbied for a new playground.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with the area where you live or the place you are talking about
examples: We buy our vegetables at the local farmers' market.
The story was covered by the local news.

senses.def: affecting only one part of the body
examples: The dentist gave me a local anesthetic.

senses.def: a person who lives in a particular place
examples: Ask the locals where the best restaurants are.

note: Trap: "local" doesn't mean "lokal" (restaurant/club) as in Turkish. "The local" in British English = the nearby pub.

senses.def: to find the exact position of someone or something
examples: Rescuers managed to locate the missing hikers.
Police used phone data to locate the suspect.

senses.def: to put or build something in a particular place
examples: The company decided to locate its new factory near the port.

senses.def: existing or situated in a particular place
examples: The hotel is conveniently located near the airport.
Our office is located on the third floor.

note: Used after "be": The museum is located downtown (= Müze şehir merkezinde yer alıyor).

senses.def: a place where something happens or exists, or the position of something
examples: The restaurant is in a great location near the river.
Turn on your phone's location services to use the map.

senses.def: a place outside a studio where a film is made
examples: The movie was shot on location in Morocco.

senses.def: a device that keeps a door, box, etc. closed, usually opened with a key
examples: Someone broke the lock on the back door.
I heard the key turn in the lock.

senses.def: to close something with a lock, or to be able to be closed in this way
examples: Did you remember to lock the car?
The screen locks automatically after five minutes.

note: "Lock yourself out" = accidentally leave your keys inside and be unable to get in.

senses.def: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree or fallen from it
examples: Put another log on the fire.
We sat on a log by the river and ate our sandwiches.

senses.def: an official written record of events, especially on a ship or aircraft
examples: The captain kept a detailed log of the voyage.

senses.def: to officially record information or events
examples: All customer calls are logged for training purposes.
I log my workouts in an app.

note: "Log in/on" = enter a computer system with a password. "Sleep like a log" = sleep very deeply.

senses.def: a reasonable way of thinking about or explaining something
examples: I don't understand the logic behind the new rules.
There's no logic in spending money we don't have.

senses.def: the formal study of reasoning and argument
examples: She took a course in logic and philosophy.

senses.def: seeming natural, reasonable or sensible
examples: It's the logical choice, since she has the most experience.
The logical next step is to test the product with users.

senses.def: following the rules of logic
examples: He laid out his argument in a clear, logical way.

senses.def: a design or symbol that a company or organization uses to identify itself
examples: The company's logo is printed on every product.
They hired a designer to create a new logo.

senses.def: unhappy because you have no friends or nobody to talk to
examples: She felt lonely after moving to a new city.
Many elderly people are lonely and isolated.

senses.def: far from other places and with few people
examples: We drove for hours along a lonely desert road.

note: "Alone" = without others (neutral); "lonely" = sad because you are alone. You can be alone but not lonely.
